jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description: Job Summary Meet the Team The Cisco cnBNG Control Plane team builds Ciscos cloud-native Broadband Network Gateway - the carrier-grade subscriber-management brain that runs as microservices on the SMI (Subscriber Microservices Infrastructure) / Kubernetes platform and interworks with IOS-XR, Silicon One-based User Plane Functions (UPFs). We power some of the worlds largest residential and business broadband deployments, serving millions of subscribers with strict availability and scale requirements. We value technical depth, automation-first engineering, continuous learning, collaborative problem-solving, and responsible adoption of AI-assisted development practices. Your Impact As a Software Engineer on the cnBNG Control Plane, you will own the design, delivery, and end-to-end quality of carrier-grade subscriber-management features in a cloud-native architecture. You will build session-handling, CP-UP separation, redundancy, and scale capabilities that keep millions of subscribers online across Silicon One-based UPFs - and own their unit, integration, system, and scale validation with automation-first practices. You will mentor junior engineers and use modern AI-assisted tools to accelerate development, testing, and debugging. What You Will Do Design, develop, and maintain cnBNG Control Plane microservices (C/C++/Go) on the SMI/Kubernetes platform, interworking with IOS-XR / Silicon One-based User Plane Functions. Implement and enhance subscriber-management functionality: PPPoE/IPoE session bring-up, DHCPv4/DHCPv6 (server/proxy/relay), Prefix Delegation, RADIUS/AAA, PAP/CHAP, accounting, Change of Authorization, IPAM, subscriber policy, and QoS. Develop and harden CP-UP separation over the State Control Interface - session programming, state download/replay, and reconciliation between the Control Plane and Silicon One UPFs. Build features for scale and high availability: cluster upscale, N:M and geo/warm redundancy (SRG), CP-GR switchover, and subscriber-session continuity during CP-UP communication failures. Own quality end-to-end: write unit tests and component/integration tests; design and execute system, regression, scale, performance, resiliency, and high-availability tests for your features. Develop reusable, scalable test automation (Python; pyATS/Genie or equivalent) and integrate it into CI/CD pipelines and regression suites. Build and maintain containerized / virtual / cloud-based test environments (Docker, Kubernetes, SMI) and validate subscriber-scale, traffic, failover, upgrade/rollback, process-restart, and subscriber-churn scenarios. Optimize control-plane performance, memory, and convergence for millions of subscribers across large UPF fleets. Develop and maintain gRPC/REST APIs and YANG/OpenConfig models, plus CLI and model-driven telemetry for configuration and operational visibility. Troubleshoot complex, distributed issues across CP, Silicon One UPFs, and the SMI/Kubernetes stack; drive RCA using logs, traces, core dumps, RADIUS transactions, and telemetry. Manage code with Git; participate in code reviews; collaborate with Test Engineering on feature, scale, and HA validation. Work with architects, DE/DT leads, and PLM to deliver features across the release lifecycle (BC/CC, AC/EC, DEVELOPING, FCS). Actively use approved AI coding assistants and engineering agents for code generation, unit/automation test creation, static analysis, log analysis, defect triage, and documentation - validating AI-generated output responsibly. Minimum Qualifications (Must-Have) Bachelors or masters degree in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Telecommunications, or a related field. Experience in systems/embedded or cloud-native software engineering for networking products. Strong programming in C/C++ and/or Go on Linux; Python for test automation and scripting. Hands-on experience writing unit, integration, system, and scale/performance tests, and building automation (pyATS/Genie or equivalent) integrated into CI/CD and regression pipelines. Solid understanding of IP networking and subscriber/broadband protocols: PPPoE, IPoE, DHCPv4/v6, RADIUS/AAA, PPP, L2TP. Working knowledge of Cisco Silicon One (SiOne) NPU-based User Plane Functions (UPFs) - data-plane/forwarding architecture, CP-to-UPF programming, and how subscriber sessions map to NPU forwarding. Cloud-native fundamentals: Docker, Kubernetes, microservices, and service meshes. Experience building and consuming gRPC/REST APIs and data models (YANG, protobuf). Distributed-systems concepts: high availability, redundancy, state reconciliation, and scale. Strong Linux skills; experience with Git, code reviews, debugging, and CI/CD pipelines. AI-assisted engineering is a must: hands-on use of AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot) and a working understanding of generative AI, AI agents, MCP (Model Context Protocol), reusable AI skills, prompt/context management, and responsible validation of AI-generated output. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on with BNG/CUPS, CP-UP separation, SRG geo/warm redundancy, or 5G/BNG converged-core architectures. Experience with SMI (Subscriber Microservices Infrastructure) or similar cloud-native telco platforms. Familiarity with Silicon One platform families (Cisco 8000 / ASR 9000 / NCS) as User Planes. Scale/performance characterization and traffic/subscriber-simulation tools (IXIA/Spirent). Databases/caching for network state (SQL/NoSQL, key-value stores, etcd); AAA/policy, IPAM at scale, and QoS. Model-driven telemetry, NETCONF/RESTCONF/gNMI, OpenConfig; Aha/Jira API suites. Expectations The successful candidate will independently own a significant Control Plane feature area and its unit/integration/system/scale validation and automation, deliver production-quality code and tests, lead complex investigations across CP and Silicon One UPFs, and provide evidence-based release recommendations - while influencing design, mentoring, and using AI-assisted tools responsibly with security and engineering accountability. jobs.title: Lead AI Engineer
jobs.description: Job Summary Position Summary: We are looking for a Lead AI Engineer in Bangalore to help build Messaging 3.0, our next-generation intelligent patient communication platform. You will design and build production-grade AI agents end to end - from LLM orchestration, tool integration, and evaluation to guardrails, observability, reliability, and production operations. You will also be the technical lead for this initiative, setting the technical direction and mentoring engineers through influence rather than formal authority. In your first 90 days, you will help establish the foundation for the AI-driven Intelligent Messaging platform, including core services, supporting services, Temporal workflows, and two initial agents: the Notification AI Agent and Cadence Outreach AI Agent. Over your first year, you will take these agents to production and build next-best-action intelligence so they can act autonomously and reliably toward the intended outcome of each message. You will also ensure the new architecture continues to support the important use cases handled by our existing legacy monolith and microservices. About the Team: The Messaging team is building Messaging 3.0 - moving from static notifications and campaign-based outreach to intelligent, agent-orchestrated patient communication. Our AI agents will use patient context, preferences, workflow state, and tools to: Determine the next best action. Personalize patient communication. Select the right communication channel. Manage the interaction through to completion. This is a mix of greenfield and brownfield development. You will build new services while also replacing or wrapping existing systems that support live patient messaging in production today. Responsibilities Essential Job Responsibilities Lead the technical design and development of the Messaging 3.0 AI platform. Build production-grade AI agents using LLM orchestration, tools, context, evaluation, guardrails, and observability. Design and build scalable services using Java, Spring Boot, microservices, Kubernetes, and AWS. Design and implement Temporal workflows for long-running and failure-prone processes, including retries and compensation. Build and take the Notification AI Agent and Cadence Outreach AI Agent to production. Build next-best-action intelligence that enables agents to act autonomously and predictably toward the intended message outcome. Identify and solve AI agent reliability and unpredictability issues in production. Ensure the new architecture continues to cover use cases supported by the existing legacy monolith and microservices. Drive high-quality delivery and continuously improve engineering speed, quality, and reliability. Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers through influence rather than formal authority. Additional Job Responsibilities Work across both greenfield and brownfield systems. Collaborate with engineers and stakeholders to establish technical direction and alignment. Own technical outcomes end to end, from design through production. Adapt as requirements and the architecture evolve. Evaluate and adopt new AI and agent technologies as the space changes. Build systems that are reliable and predictable in production, not just successful in demos. Understand existing messaging systems well enough to avoid gaps in functionality during modernization. Qualifications 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ years building AI agents. Strong hands-on experience with Java and Spring Boot in production. Strong system design and software architecture experience, including architectural trade-offs and decision-making. Production experience deploying and operating services on Kubernetes. Experience with Temporal or an equivalent durable workflow orchestration framework. Hands-on experience with LangGraph, LangChain, or an equivalent agent framework. Experience taking an AI/agentic system from prototype to reliable production. Strong understanding of AI/agent engineering, including reliability, evaluation, guardrails, and observability. Production experience with AWS and practical experience making AWS architecture decisions. Experience with Kafka, Postgres, Redis, Helm, Datadog, or equivalent observability tools is a plus. Data science experience is a plus. GenAI experience beyond agent frameworks, such as prompt/model evaluation or fine-tuning, is a plus. Strong communication, collaboration, and technical leadership skills. Comfortable working in ambiguous and evolving environments and leading through influence. 8-13 Yrs Healthcare, Architecture, Microservices, Tools, Cadence, Messaging Systems, Data, Campaigns

Internal applications: Small, purpose-built web applications where no off-the-shelf tool fits, built end to end — React or Angular front end, Python/C#/Node API, SQL database — secured with CAI's identity platform. Proficiency in a back-end language (Python, C#/.NET or Node.js/TypeScript), a modern front-end framework (React or Angular) and SQL, including data modeling and query tuning. Dashboards and data pipelines: Power BI, Tableau or a code-based stack; ETL/ELT design; API integration with SaaS business applications (OAuth 2.0, webhooks, incremental extraction) — ideally two or more of NetSuite, Salesforce/Service Cloud, Gong, Mosaic, Aha!, Jira/ADO, GitHub. Business instinct to pick problems worth solving, clear written and spoken English with non-technical stakeholders, strong self-direction across concurrent projects, and regular overlap with US business hours. Priorities and assignments from the GM, CAI Discrete Manufacturing; engineering standards and cross-BU practice with the Director of Engineering, Bangalore. Instrument automations with observability and tracing so failures, cost spikes, latency regressions, and quality drift are detected early. Implement human-in-the-loop checkpoints, approval steps, and safe fallbacks for workflows where full autonomy is inappropriate. Optimize for cost and latency through model selection, caching, batching, prompt compression, and routing between larger and smaller models. Document architecture, runbooks, and handover material; support and iterate on automations after launch. Follow security, privacy, and responsible-AI requirements around data handling, access control, PII, and model usage. Practical experience with LLM APIs (e.g. Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Bedrock) in a real application, not just experimentation. Hands-on experience with at least one agent or orchestration framework (LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, or equivalent in-house tooling). Demonstrated experience building RAG systems and working with a vector store (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, OpenSearch, or similar). Solid grasp of prompt engineering and context design, plus structured output techniques (JSON schemas, tool/function calling, validation and repair). Familiarity with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) - building MCP servers to expose internal systems as agent tools, and integrating them into agent applications. Working knowledge of SQL and data modeling; comfortable joining and cleaning data across systems. Experience with Git-based workflows, code review, and CI/CD. Cloud experience on AWS, Azure, or GCP - compute, serverless functions, queues, secrets management, and managed AI services. Containerization fundamentals with Docker. Proven ability to work directly with stakeholders: eliciting requirements, demoing prototypes, and managing expectations. Multi-agent system design - planner/executor patterns, supervisor architectures, delegation, and shared state. Document intelligence and multimodal work: OCR, PDF parsing, table extraction, vision model usage. Frontend familiarity (React.js, Next.js, TypeScript) for building internal tools and demos. Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, CloudFormation) and Kubernetes exposure. Experience with enterprise governance concerns: AI risk review, audit trails, data residency, and access-scoped retrieval.
